title: How a C# program works — quick overview
rememberThis: C# compiles to Intermediate Language (IL) for the Common Language Runtime (CLR). TypeScript only checks types, then erases them into JavaScript.
Your project file sets the Target Framework Moniker (TFM). .NET 10 means C# 14. Avoid LangVersion=latest.
One entry point per app: a static Main method or top-level statements in exactly one file.
File-based apps (dotnet run file.cs) use C# 14 #: directives instead of a .csproj — great for quick scripts.
bullets: The Common Type System (CTS) is the shared type model; the CLR is the run-time host — not Node.js or V8.
Assemblies (.dll) are deployment units with IL and metadata — not the same as JavaScript ES modules.
using statements shorten type names; NuGet packages and project references still supply the actual code.
Implicit usings auto-generate global using lines so new console apps need fewer imports.
